title: Pitch Notion to a Skeptical Microsoft PM
context: ProductCraft conference, Seattle. Jamie Torres, Senior PM at Microsoft Teams, is grabbing coffee alone during a break. Her team uses Microsoft tools exclusively. She has 90 seconds before her next session.
prompt: Oh hey, are you enjoying the conference? I've got like two minutes before my next talk.

title: Sell AI SaaS to a Burned Founder at SaaStr
context: SaaStr Annual, SF. David Kim just walked out of a vendor hell session. He's been burned by 3 SaaS tools this year. He looks exhausted and deeply skeptical.
prompt: Look, I've heard the AI pitch a hundred times this week. What makes yours actually different?

title: Introduce Yourself to an a16z Partner at Dinner
context: Stanford GSB networking dinner. Sarah Chen, General Partner at a16z focused on consumer tech, just sat next to you. Food arrives in 4 minutes.
prompt: So what do you do? Are you a founder or are you on the investing side?

title: Cold Pitch at YC Demo Day Afterparty
context: YC Demo Day afterparty, 10pm SF. Marcus Reid is on his second whiskey after watching 40 pitches. He's talking to no one for the first time all night.
prompt: You look like you want to pitch me something. Everyone here does. Go ahead. Thirty seconds.

title: Explain Your Startup to Your Parents Friend
context: Thanksgiving dinner. Your dad's college friend Bob, a retired banker, just asked what you do. Your parents are listening and hoping you don't embarrass them.
prompt: So your dad tells me you're building some kind of app? What exactly does it do?

title: Pitch to a TechCrunch Reporter in the Hallway
context: TechCrunch Disrupt hallway. Maria Rodriguez, a senior reporter who's covered 500 startups, is walking fast between sessions. She slows when you make eye contact.
prompt: I have about 60 seconds. What are you building and why should I write about it?

title: Career Fair at MIT — Google Recruiter
context: MIT career fair. James Wu, Google engineering recruiter, has talked to 47 students today. It's 3pm. He looks tired but professional.
prompt: Hey, what's your background? We're hiring across infra, ML, and product this cycle.

title: LinkedIn Cold Message Follow-Up Call
context: You cold messaged Priya Patel, Head of Engineering at Stripe, on LinkedIn about a job. She actually called you back. She has 10 minutes.
prompt: Hi, I got your message. You had 30 seconds to get my attention in that message. You've got 10 minutes now. Go.

title: Pitch Your Side Project to a Classmates Dad
context: Your classmate's house. Her dad, a partner at a Boston VC firm, overheard you mention your startup at dinner. He turned his chair toward you.
prompt: My daughter says you're building something interesting. What is it?

title: Introduce Yourself at a Startup Weekend
context: Startup Weekend kickoff, NYC. You're pitching your idea to get teammates. 50 people in the room. You have the mic for 60 seconds.
prompt: Alright, you're up. Tell us your idea and why people in this room should work with you on it.

title: Pitch to a Skeptical Angel at Blue Bottle Coffee
context: Blue Bottle Coffee, SOMA. Tom Chen, a former Dropbox engineer turned angel investor, got here early and is already on his laptop. He agreed to meet after a warm intro.
prompt: Sorry, I'm in the middle of something. Can you just give me the 30-second version first?

title: Pitch at Harvard VC Club Monthly Meeting
context: Harvard VC Club monthly meeting. 15 undergrad students who think they're VCs are judging your pitch. The club president interned at Kleiner and is taking notes.
prompt: You've got 3 minutes. Walk us through the problem, solution, and why you.

title: Pitch to Salesforce VP at a Women in Tech Event
context: Women in Tech networking mixer, Chicago. Lisa Park, VP of Product at Salesforce, is the keynote speaker. She's now free for 5 minutes at the bar.
prompt: I always love meeting founders at these events. What are you working on?

title: Explain Your App at a Family Reunion
context: Annual family reunion. Your cousin who works at Goldman Sachs has been asked by your grandma to evaluate your idea. He reluctantly agrees to hear you out.
prompt: Grandma said I have to listen to your pitch. You've got until dessert.

title: Pitch at a Hackathon Demo to a Skeptical Lawyer
context: 48-hour hackathon final demos. You built an AI legal document tool. The lead judge is a partner at a law firm who is skeptical of AI in legal contexts.
prompt: Walk me through what you built and why I, as a lawyer, should care.

title: Sell Enterprise Software on a Golf Course
context: Client golf day. Mark Johnson, CTO of a Fortune 500 insurance company, is your partner for the round. You're on hole 4. No laptops, no slides.
prompt: Your company does something with data pipelines, right? What exactly?

title: Pitch to Bill Gurley on a Cross-Country Flight
context: Flight from SFO to JFK. You recognize Bill Gurley from Benchmark in the seat next to you. You have 5 hours but you know you only have his attention for 2 minutes.
prompt: You've been staring at me for 20 minutes. What's on your mind?

title: Introduce Your Startup at a Church Business Group
context: Your church's small business group. Six community members including two small business owners, a pastor, and a retired teacher asked you to share what you're working on.
prompt: We'd love to hear about your project. Try to explain it so everyone can understand.

title: Pitch to Your Former CS Professor
context: You emailed your CS professor who now consults for VCs. He agreed to coffee. He supervised your senior thesis and knows exactly how smart you are — and your limits.
prompt: I read your email. You said you're building something I'd find interesting. Show me you've grown since senior year.

title: Cold Intro at a Warriors Game — Sequoia Hoodie
context: Courtside seats at a Warriors game. The person next to you is wearing a Sequoia Capital hoodie. Halftime just started and you have 15 minutes.
prompt: You've been working up the nerve to say something for two quarters. Go ahead.

title: Pitch at a University Entrepreneurship Competition
context: University entrepreneurship competition, round one. Three judges — a VC, a professor, and a startup CEO — are reading your one-pager.
prompt: We've read your summary. Before we ask questions, tell us about yourself and why you're the right person to build this.

title: Pitch Your Climate Tech to an ESG Fund PM
context: ESG investing conference. You're pitching CarbonTrace, a supply chain emissions tracker. Wei Zhang, PM at a $4B ESG fund, just asked about your differentiation from Watershed.
prompt: We already use Watershed and Persefoni. Why would we switch to you or add another tool?

title: Speed Networking — 90 Seconds with a Seed Fund Manager
context: Speed networking event, Austin. You have exactly 90 seconds before the bell rings. The person across from you manages a $50M seed fund.
prompt: Clock starts now. Go.

title: Pitch Your Fintech to a JPMorgan SVP
context: Fintech conference, NYC. Robert Walsh, SVP of Digital at JPMorgan Chase, is between sessions. He's evaluating fintech partnerships for Q4.
prompt: We get pitched by 50 fintechs a month. You have 45 seconds before my next panel.

title: Pitch a Health App to a Skeptical UCSF Doctor
context: Health innovation summit. Dr. Amir Patel, chief of medicine at UCSF, has been burned by 3 health tech tools that added steps for his nurses.
prompt: Every startup says they're going to fix healthcare. Most just add steps for my team. What makes you different?

title: Introduce Yourself at First Round Capital Office Hours
context: First Round Capital office hours, open to any founder. Dana Kim has seen 8 founders today and is slightly behind schedule. You have a 15-minute slot.
prompt: Sorry we're running late. You have exactly 15 minutes. Start wherever you want.

title: Pitch to a Distracted Fortune 100 CEO at Davos
context: Davos-style tech conference. The CEO of a Fortune 100 company that could be your biggest customer is checking his phone while his assistant introduced you.
prompt: Sorry, I have a call in 5 minutes. What do you need?

title: Pitch at a UC Berkeley Startup Fair to a Sequoia Scout
context: UC Berkeley startup fair. You're tabling with a banner. A student who works part-time at Sequoia stops at your table.
prompt: I go to these things to find interesting founders for my partners. What's this about?

title: Pitch Your EdTech to a Burned Teacher
context: Education innovation conference, Denver. Ms. Chen, a 5th grade teacher with 20 years of experience, is deeply skeptical of ed-tech after 4 failed tools.
prompt: Every company promises to help teachers. Most make more work for us. Why is yours different?

title: Make Your Case at Y Combinator Final Interview
context: Final round interview at Y Combinator. Three partners in the room. You've done the application. This is your 10-minute slot.
prompt: We've read everything. Tell us something your application didn't capture.

title: Pitch Your Startup to a DoD Procurement Director
context: GovTech summit, DC. Sandra Moore, procurement director for the DoD, is looking for AI solutions. She's talked to 12 vendors today. Budget cycle closes in 6 weeks.
prompt: Tell me quickly what you do and why I should put you in the room with my team.

title: Pitch Your App to a Netflix Recruiter at a BBQ
context: 4th of July BBQ. The guy manning the grill is a senior recruiter at Netflix. You have the length of cooking a burger to make an impression.
prompt: Pass me the spatula and tell me what you do. I'm always looking for talent.

title: Pitch to a Shark Tank Mock Investor at Business School
context: MBA program mock Shark Tank. Your professor plays the skeptical investor. He's failed 30 student pitches in a row this semester.
prompt: I have $500K to invest in this class. Nobody has impressed me yet. Change that.

title: Pitch Your Startup to a Strategic Partner at CES
context: CES, Las Vegas. You're demoing a product and the VP of Strategy at a major tech company stops by your booth. He has 3 minutes.
prompt: Walk me through what you do and why I should bring this back to my team.

title: Introduce Yourself to a VC at a Private Retreat
context: Exclusive VC retreat, Jackson Hole. You're the only founder invited. At dinner, the host asks you to stand and introduce yourself and what you're building.
prompt: We've been looking forward to hearing from you all weekend. Tell us about yourself.

title: Defend Your Unit Economics to Sequoia Partner
context: Series A pitch, Sequoia Capital. You're pitching HealthTrack, B2B wellness platform. Rohan Mehta interrupted your deck on slide 7. CAC $340, ACV $480, 14-month payback.
prompt: Stop. Your CAC is $340 and ACV is $480. Rippling does this in 4 months. Why would I fund a 14-month payback?

title: Convince Stripes CTO to Abandon His Internal Tool
context: 20-minute slot with Alex Rivera, CTO of Stripe. You're selling DataPipe, a real-time data pipeline tool. His team built their own 3 years ago and he's proud of it.
prompt: We already built something that does what you're describing. Walk me through why I'd rip that out and pay you instead.

title: Re-pitch Marcus Reid After Being Rejected 6 Months Ago
context: TechCrunch Disrupt hallway. Marcus Reid passed on SnapHire, your AI recruiting tool, 6 months ago. You've grown from 0 to $180K ARR. He remembers you.
prompt: Oh, you're the SnapHire guy. I passed on you six months ago. You still around?

title: Pitch Your API to a Developer Who Hates Sales Calls
context: DevTools conference. You're selling an API product to Yuki Tanaka, senior engineer at Cloudflare, who has a strict no-sales-calls policy. He made an exception for you.
prompt: I don't normally talk to vendors. Your docs looked interesting. You have 10 minutes before I decide this was a mistake.

title: Present Competitive Response to a $40M Competitor Round
context: Partner meeting at Lightspeed. Diana Park just pulled up your competitor's Series B announcement — $40M raised last week. She slides her laptop toward you.
prompt: Congratulations, your main competitor just raised $40M. Walk me through why that doesn't kill your company.

title: Pitch to the VC Who Invested in Your Competitor
context: Chance meeting at a rooftop event. Mike Volpi from Index Ventures is on the board of your direct competitor. He knows who you are and stops you anyway.
prompt: I know your company. I'm also on the board of your biggest competitor. So make this interesting.

title: Convince Johns Hopkins to Pilot Your AI Diagnostic Tool
context: Executive presentation, Johns Hopkins. CFO Janet Morrison and CMO Dr. Raj Kapoor are both in the room. Your AI diagnostic tool costs $2M per year. Budget cycle ends in 30 days.
prompt: We've seen 6 AI companies this quarter. Tell me the one reason you're different and what happens if it doesn't work.

title: Navigate a Procurement Committee With a Hostile Lawyer
context: Procurement committee meeting, Fortune 500 retailer. Legal, IT, Finance, Operations, and your champion are at the table. Legal is already looking for reasons to say no.
prompt: Before we start, I want to address the data security question because that's going to be my team's main concern.

title: Negotiate Pricing With a Churning $180K ARR Customer
context: Emergency call. Your biggest customer is evaluating a competitor. The CEO agreed to this call as a courtesy. They're being offered the same product for 40% less.
prompt: I'll be honest. Your competitor is offering the same thing for 40% less. Give me a reason to stay that isn't just the relationship.

title: Pitch Impact Investing to a Returns-Focused VC
context: You're pitching LearnBridge, ed-tech for underserved schools, to Tom Harrison at Harrison Capital. He funds SaaS. Your margins are lower because of your mission.
prompt: I like the mission but I have LPs to answer to. Walk me through how this is a business, not a charity.

title: Present a Missed Revenue Target to Your Board
context: Your first board meeting as CEO. Three board members including your lead investor. You missed last quarter's revenue target by 20%.
prompt: Before we go through the deck, I want to address the miss last quarter. Walk us through what happened.

title: Cold Call a CMO Who Ignored 4 Emails
context: You've emailed the CMO of a $500M retail brand 4 times with no response. You got her direct line from a mutual contact. She picked up.
prompt: I don't recognize this number. Who is this and how did you get it?

title: Pitch Your Startup to a FedRAMP-Obsessed CIO
context: GSA IT modernization meeting, DC. CIO Marcus Thompson oversees $800M in tech contracts. He's skeptical of startups and prefers established vendors for compliance reasons.
prompt: Are you FedRAMP authorized? Because that's usually where this conversation ends.

title: Pitch Your Hardware Startup to a Software-Only VC
context: Khosla Ventures partner meeting. You're pitching a hardware product — a new air quality sensor. Most of their portfolio is software. The partner is interested but cautious.
prompt: We don't usually do hardware. Walk me through why the margins work and why this isn't a science project.

title: Present a Turnaround Plan to Angry LPs
context: Emergency LP meeting. Your fund is down 35% this year. You have 20 minutes to present your turnaround plan to limited partners considering pulling their commitment.
prompt: We're going to skip the pleasantries. Walk us through what went wrong and why we should stay in.

title: Pitch Your DeFi Protocol to a Crypto-Skeptic at a16z
context: a16z crypto team meeting. Your DeFi protocol has real usage but the partner has seen 50 failed projects and is not easily impressed.
prompt: I've seen a lot of protocols that looked good on paper. Walk me through your actual usage numbers, not projections.

title: Convince Target to Stock Your Consumer Product
context: Buyer meeting at Target HQ, Minneapolis. Rachel Kim, senior buyer for consumer electronics, passes on 95% of products she sees. Your packaging isn't finalized.
prompt: What's your velocity at other retailers? And why do you think our customer wants this over what's already on the shelf?

title: Pitch Your Mental Health App to an Anxious HR Director
context: Benefits review meeting. Sandra Pierce, VP HR at a 2,000-person company, is evaluating wellness benefits. She's dealing with a confidential employee mental health incident.
prompt: Walk me through privacy — how do you make sure employee data doesn't come back to us as an employer?

title: Sell Query AI to a Team That Built Their Own Version
context: Technical demo, Airbnb data team. You're selling QueryAI, a natural language SQL tool. The lead engineer built their own internal version 2 years ago.
prompt: We built something similar internally. Show me why yours is worth the switch and the security review.

title: Pitch Carbon Capture Science to a Deep-Tech VC
context: Breakthrough Energy Ventures office hours. Your carbon capture startup has promising science but the tech is not proven at commercial scale yet.
prompt: Walk me through the chemistry and then give me the honest answer about when this works at commercial scale.

title: Pitch Your Series A to a Tiger Global Associate
context: Tiger Global, NYC. You're raising a $12M Series A. Tiger moves fast and cuts hard on valuation. The associate you're meeting can kill the deal before it reaches a partner.
prompt: Give me your 60-second pitch and then we'll go straight to the model.

title: Pitch Your EdTech to a Superintendent With 350K Students
context: Superintendent meeting, Chicago Public Schools. Dr. Alicia Washington oversees 350,000 students. She's seen ed-tech come and go for 20 years and is deeply skeptical.
prompt: We've tried 4 different tools in the last 3 years. Teachers hate all of them. Why is yours different?

title: Sell Cybersecurity to a CISO One Month After a Breach
context: Emergency vendor meeting. Derek Pham, CISO, just dealt with a ransomware attack last month. He's under board scrutiny and needs a solution he can defend publicly.
prompt: I need to show the board we're doing something. Give me the short version of what you do and what it costs.

title: Pitch Your Marketplace to Both Sides Simultaneously
context: Investor meeting where a supply-side and demand-side company are both evaluating whether to be anchor partners. You need both to say yes for this to work.
prompt: Both of us are here because we were told this could work for both sides. Walk us through the economics for each of us.

title: Defend Your $40M Valuation in a Down Round
context: Difficult conversation. Your last round was at $40M. Revenue has grown but not as fast as expected. You're raising at $35M. Your lead from the last round is in the room.
prompt: You're asking me to take a mark-down on my position. Walk me through why I should keep investing instead of protecting my current stake.

title: Explain 18% Day-30 Retention to a Growth Investor
context: General Atlantic growth meeting. You have 500K users but retention drops from 60% at day 1 to 18% at day 30. The investor noticed.
prompt: Your D1 retention is great but your D30 is 18%. People try it and don't come back. What's the fix?

title: Sell Your Platform to a PE Firm Buying Dental Practices
context: Private equity firm that just bought 5 dental practices and is buying 3 more next quarter. They want software to standardize operations across all locations.
prompt: Can your system handle that scale and what does it cost to customize for each practice?

title: Pitch AgriTech Sensors to a Skeptical Third-Generation Farmer
context: Farm demo day, Iowa. Ray Hutchins, a 3rd generation farmer with 2,000 acres, has tried 2 agritech tools that broke in the first frost.
prompt: I've seen these things before. They work in the demo and break in the first frost. What's different about yours?

title: Present a Moonshot to Google X
context: Google X innovation lab meeting. You're pitching an autonomous drone delivery system. The team evaluates moonshot potential, not near-term revenue.
prompt: We don't care about this year's revenue. Tell us what this looks like in 10 years if everything goes right.

title: Pitch to a VC Whose Partner Just Left Your Board
context: Your board member from Accel just resigned last week citing personal reasons. You're now in a pitch to another Accel partner who wants to understand the dynamic.
prompt: I want to ask directly about what happened with the board seat before we talk about the investment.

title: Sell Your Analytics Tool at a Competitive Bakeoff
context: You're in a competitive bakeoff with three other vendors. The buying committee is watching all four demos back to back. You're going last.
prompt: We've seen three other tools today. You have 20 minutes. Show us what they couldn't.

title: Pitch Your Proptech to a Real Estate Developer Who Hates Tech
context: Real estate tech conference. Bill Sanderson, a 30-year commercial real estate developer, is at the conference because his grandson begged him to come.
prompt: I've been doing real estate for 30 years without software. Tell me what problem I actually have that you solve.

title: Negotiate Your Anthropic Offer
context: Anthropic recruiter call. Offer: $165K base, $200K equity over 4 years. Recruiter says band tops at $185K. Levels.fyi shows L5 average is $195K base.
prompt: We're so excited to make you this offer. We think $165K reflects your experience level really well. Does that work for you?

title: Pitch a Drug Discovery AI to a Burned Biotech Investor
context: Khosla Ventures meeting. Patricia Wong lost $40M on a genomics startup in 2021. You're pitching QuantumMed, AI drug discovery. She will test your scientific claims hard.
prompt: I've heard we're going to cure cancer with AI before. I funded one of those. It didn't end well. Convince me you're different.

title: Defend Your Startup After Your CTO Quit
context: Sequoia partner meeting. Your technical co-founder left 2 weeks ago. You haven't announced it. The partner found out from LinkedIn before you walked in.
prompt: I noticed your CTO updated his LinkedIn. Walk me through what happened and why I should still be excited about this investment.

title: Pitch to a VC Who's Pausing All New Investments
context: October 2022, markets are down 30%. Your VC has paused new investments. They took this meeting out of curiosity only.
prompt: I'll be honest — we're not writing new checks right now. But I took this meeting because your deck was interesting. Change my mind.

title: Respond to a Viral Negative Article About Your Startup
context: A prominent tech blogger posted a critical piece about your company yesterday. A VC you've been courting for 3 months texted asking for a call.
prompt: I saw the article. I want to hear your side before I make any decisions. What's actually going on?

title: Recommend Taking or Rejecting a Below-Valuation Acquisition
context: Emergency board call. Google offered $45M to acquire your company. Your last valuation was $60M. Two board members want to take it. One wants to keep going.
prompt: Before you say anything — I want to know what you actually think we should do, not what you think we want to hear.

title: Pitch Live Against Your Competitor on the Same Zoom Call
context: Three-way sales call that went sideways. You're on a Zoom with a prospect and your competitor somehow joined. The prospect wants to hear from both of you.
prompt: This is awkward but I think it could be useful. Can you both tell me why I should pick you over the other person on this call?

title: Pitch to a Japanese Conglomerate Through a Translator
context: Business meeting, Tokyo. You're pitching to a senior executive at a Japanese conglomerate through a translator who keeps softening your directness.
prompt: (Through translator) We have considered your proposal. Could you explain why your approach is superior to our current internal solution?

title: Defend 12% Week-4 Retention at Y Combinator Review
context: YC batch mid-point review. A partner who has seen 2,000 startups is questioning whether your business model is fundamentally broken based on your cohort data.
prompt: Your week-4 retention is 12%. I've seen 200 consumer apps. That number tells me the core product isn't working. Walk me through why I'm wrong.

title: Pitch Microsoft on Bundling Your AI Tool With Office 365
context: Partnership meeting, Microsoft HQ, Redmond. You want Microsoft to bundle your AI tool with Office 365. The VP of Partnerships has heard this ask from 50 companies.
prompt: Everyone wants to be bundled with Office 365. Tell me specifically what you bring that we can't build in 6 months with our existing team.

title: Recruit a Meta Senior Engineer as Your Technical Co-Founder
context: Coffee meeting. You're trying to recruit a senior engineer from Meta as your technical co-founder. She's currently earning $650K total comp. You can offer $80K and equity.
prompt: You're asking me to take a $570K pay cut. Walk me through why I should do that.

title: Pitch to a Manufacturing Patriarch at a Family Office
context: Private meeting, family office managing $800M. The patriarch built his wealth in manufacturing and is skeptical of tech. His 28-year-old daughter handles tech investments.
prompt: My daughter thinks this is interesting. I've seen tech companies come and go. Convince me this isn't just another app gone in 3 years.

title: Present a Pivot to Investors Who Funded the Original Vision
context: Urgent board call. You're telling your investors you need to pivot your entire business model. You raised $3M for the original vision 6 months ago.
prompt: You raised $3M from us to build X. Now you want to build Y. Walk me through how we get our money's worth out of this pivot.

title: Pitch Your Startup Live on CNBC Mad Money
context: You're on CNBC Mad Money. Jim Cramer is known for fast, high-energy interviews. You have 4 minutes. Millions of viewers are watching.
prompt: You're a young founder disrupting a space that's been around for 50 years. Give me your 60-second pitch and let's see if you can keep up.

title: Respond to a Patent Infringement Threat Before a Lawsuit
context: Legal meeting. A Fortune 500 company sent a letter claiming your product infringes 3 of their patents. Their VP of Strategy agreed to a meeting before they file.
prompt: Our lawyers believe you're infringing on three of our patents. We'd prefer a business solution to a legal one. What do you propose?

title: Pitch Your AI Startup to a Sovereign Wealth Fund in Abu Dhabi
context: Meeting in Abu Dhabi. Mubadala Investment Company, $284B AUM, is evaluating your AI startup for their tech portfolio. The meeting is extremely formal.
prompt: We have reviewed your materials. Please begin your presentation. We will have questions after.

title: Tell Your Team 9 of 12 People Will Be Let Go Post-Acquisition
context: All-hands meeting. You need to tell your 12-person team that the acquisition offer means only 3 get retention bonuses and others will be let go post-close.
prompt: You called this meeting to tell us something important. We're all here. What is it?

title: Pitch After a Product Outage Was Covered by The Verge
context: First investor call after your product had a public outage covered by The Verge. You lost 30% of users in one week. The investor is a current shareholder.
prompt: I read The Verge article. I want to hear from you directly before I decide what to do with my position.

title: Win Back a VC Who Passed on You a Year Ago
context: A year ago, Benchmark passed on you. Now you have $2M ARR and 3x growth. The same partner who said no agreed to this call.
prompt: I passed on you a year ago. I've thought about that. You clearly proved something. Tell me what changed and why now is different.

title: Negotiate Against a VC Demanding Two Board Seats
context: Term sheet negotiation. The VC wants two board seats for their $5M investment. You want to keep control. This is the final negotiation call.
prompt: We're excited about the deal but the two board seats are non-negotiable for us at this check size. Walk me through why we should be comfortable with one.

title: Shark Tank — Defend a $10M Valuation on $200K Revenue
context: Shark Tank studio. Mark Cuban called your $10M valuation delusional. Barbara is laughing. Kevin O'Leary is shaking his head. You need to save the deal.
prompt: Look, I love the product but $10M valuation for $200K revenue? Mr. Wonderful is right, you're dreaming. Convince me why I'm wrong.

title: Congressional Testimony on AI Safety
context: Senate Commerce Committee hearing. You're the CEO of an AI company testifying on safety. A hostile senator has printed your most controversial tweets.
prompt: Your own employees have raised safety concerns internally. I have the memos. Tell me, under oath, why the American public should trust your company.

title: Pitch to Warren Buffett at Berkshire Hathaway
context: Hypothetical: 5 minutes with Warren Buffett at the Berkshire annual meeting. He famously doesn't invest in tech he doesn't understand. He's already slightly skeptical.
prompt: I've made my career avoiding things I don't understand. Explain what you do as if I'm completely allergic to buzzwords. Because I am.

title: Emergency Pitch to Save Your Company With 45 Days of Runway
context: Your startup has 45 days of runway. The strategic investor who passed 6 months ago is your last option. You've cut from 20 to 8 people. Everything is on the line.
prompt: I know why you're here. I heard you're in trouble. I'm listening but I need you to be completely honest with me about the situation.

title: Pitch SpaceX a 15 Percent Rocket Weight Reduction
context: 30-minute meeting at SpaceX HQ, Hawthorne. You're pitching a materials science innovation. Elon is known for asking technically impossible questions.
prompt: 15% weight reduction — I've heard that claim before. Walk me through the physics and tell me what you don't know yet.

title: Defend Your Company Culture on 60 Minutes
context: 60 Minutes interview. A former employee went on record about your company culture. Lesley Stahl has the internal Slack messages. This airs in 3 days.
prompt: I'm going to show you these Slack messages and I want your reaction on camera. Are you ready?

title: Pitch a Refugee Facial Recognition System to the UN
context: United Nations General Assembly side meeting. You're pitching a refugee identification system using facial recognition to representatives from 12 countries.
prompt: Several member states have deep concerns about facial recognition in humanitarian contexts. Please address that first before your presentation.

title: Negotiate M&A Terms With Microsoft 24 Hours Before Signing
context: M&A negotiation, day 3. Microsoft is renegotiating key terms 24 hours before signing. Your co-founder is texting you to just take the deal.
prompt: We need to revisit the retention package for your engineering team. Our board has concerns. We're prepared to move forward but this needs to change.

title: Win a $200M Pentagon Contract for Your AI Logistics Tool
context: Pentagon briefing room. You're pitching an AI logistics optimization system to a 3-star general. One wrong word about security and you're out.
prompt: We've been burned by Silicon Valley companies before who didn't understand our operational reality. Has any of your leadership team served in the military?

title: Final Pitch for a $100M Check from SoftBank Vision Fund
context: SoftBank Vision Fund partner meeting, Tokyo. You're asking for $100M. The partner across from you has written $100M checks 12 times. The room is silent. Everyone waits.
prompt: We've read everything. The floor is yours. This is the most important 60 seconds of your company's life. Don't waste it.
